claims.text: As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a density of about 10.21 g/cm³.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a room-temperature yield strength of about 1600 MPa.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a high-temperature yield strength of about 855 MPa.
Replacing 10% of the Ta content with V will reduce the alloy's density by about 5%.
Replacing 10% of the Ta content with V will preserve at least 95% of baseline yield strength at room temperature.
Replacing 10% of the Ta content with V will preserve at least 95% of baseline yield strength at 1000 °C.
Partial replacement of Ta by V will maintain a solid-solution BCC matrix.
The lower atomic mass of V relative to Ta reduces the overall alloy density.
V provides solid-solution strengthening that preserves high-temperature mechanical performance in the BCC phase.
The modified alloy will have a density of approximately 9.7 g/cm³.
The modified alloy's room-temperature yield strength will remain above 1500 MPa.
The modified alloy's yield strength at 1000 °C will exceed 800 MPa.
Substitution levels above 15% V may induce detrimental phases.
Detrimental phases induced above 15% V substitution may significantly reduce high-temperature performance.
Phase stability after V addition is not fully characterized.
V addition may reduce oxidation resistance.
The mechanical-performance prediction applies under quasistatic loading between 25 and 1000 °C in inert atmosphere or vacuum.

contradictions.description: Retaining at least 95% of a 1600 MPa room-temperature baseline requires at least 1520 MPa, but the predicted threshold is only above 1500 MPa, which permits a result that violates the hypothesis and its 5% loss criterion.

Retaining at least 95% of an 855 MPa baseline at 1000 °C requires at least 812.25 MPa, but the predicted threshold is only above 800 MPa, which permits a result that would be falsified by the stated greater-than-5% strength-loss rule.
